initial_test_attempt.cause: Popen and pidfd syscalls see inner PID namespace, but /proc is mounted in an outer PID namespace. Numeric /proc/<local PID> resolved an unrelated outer process. Strict session identity validation rejected registration before signaling.
initial_test_attempt.representative_error: RuntimeError: task must be a live independent session leader

repair.proc_mapping: Require /proc/<outer>/ns/pid inode equal to /proc/self/ns/pid; map local NSpid/NSpgid/NSsid; keep outer procfs_pid for stat/environ reads.
repair.signal_identity: PID namespace inode + local PID/PGID/session + procfs PID + Linux start_time_ticks + batch/task token checked; pidfd_open(local PID), repeated identity before pidfd_send_signal.
repair.spawn_race: Child PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) and expected-parent checks before/after registration; child waits pipe gate until atomic fsynced ownership registry; rank blocks termination over spawn/registry then handles SIGTERM with finally cleanup.
repair.batch_scope: Only expected manifest task IDs under this create-only batch, matching random batch owner token. No global numeric killpg.
repair.runtime_guards_preserved: Per-task wall limit, whole-batch wall limit, memory limits, source and DATA/STATE identity checks, all three native-library pins.

cases: Own child/grandchild killed, unrelated control remains alive

sources.supports: PID file descriptor identifies process for later signaling
PID namespace permissions and pidfd signaling identity

scope_limit: Trusted Python/Fortran workers do not create new PID namespaces or alter task tokens; inaccessible identities are never signaled. This is bounded owned-session cleanup, not an arbitrary malicious descendant sandbox.
